chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-Hasan ibn Salih, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a woman who was owned by her husband (i.e., a concubine or wife) but her husband had not yet had sexual intercourse with her, and she died, leaving behind her mother, two brothers from her father and mother, her grandfather (father of her mother), and her husband. He (peace be upon him) said: 'The husband is given half, and the mother is given the remainder, and the grandfather is given nothing because his daughter (the mother) blocks him from the inheritance, and the brothers are given nothing.'

key_terms.لَمْ يَدْخُلْ بِهَا: Had not yet had sexual intercourse

ai.seo_question: How is inheritance distributed for a woman whose husband has not yet had intercourse with her?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the inheritance shares for a slave woman whose husband has not consummated the marriage, establishing that the husband receives half and the mother takes the remainder as a residual heir. It explicitly excludes the paternal grandfather and full brothers, illustrating the Shia principle of 'hijab' (blocking) where the daughter prevents the grandfather from inheriting, a key distinction in fiqh al-mirath. The ruling underscores the significance of marital consummation in determining the spouse's share and the hierarchy of heirs in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, and a number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Al Hassan Bin Salih who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about a woman whom her husband had yet to sleep with her, died, and left her mother, and her two brothers from her father and her mother (nephews), and her grandfather being father of her mother, and her husband. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘For the husband is the half, and give the remainder to the mother, and do not give anything to the grandfather, because his daughter blocks him from the inheritance, and the brothers would not be given anything (either)’.
en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad and a number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad all from ibn Mahbub from al-Hassan ibn Salih who has narrated the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a woman who is married, but before going to bed with her husband, has died leaving behind her mother, two brothers from her father and mother and her grandfather, who is the father of her mother, and her husband. He (the Imam) said, ‘The husband receives one-half and the rest belongs to her mother. The grandfather does not receive anything; his daughter bars him from inheritance and brothers do not receive anything.’”
